macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: Stocks and futures steadied as oil retreated after fresh U.S.-Iran tensions
items.summary: Reuters reported that U.S. stock index futures edged higher as oil prices eased and investors reassessed the impact of renewed U.S. strikes on Iran. The move came amid broader concern that Middle East tensions could keep inflation and bond-market volatility elevated.

items.title: European shares rose, led by a rebound in technology
items.summary: European equities gained in choppy trading as tech stocks recovered and investors continued to weigh the outlook for the conflict in the Middle East. Reuters said the market also reacted to remarks that Iran wanted to make a deal.

items.title: Asian shares climbed, but oil gains capped the rally
items.summary: Reuters said Asian markets advanced as semiconductors recovered from heavy selling, although the rally was restrained by a jump in oil prices. The rise in crude renewed inflation fears and pressured bonds.

items.title: Oil prices rose after new U.S. strikes on Iran
items.summary: Reuters reported that crude moved higher after the U.S. launched fresh strikes against Iran, reviving fears over supply disruption and the possible reopening of the Strait of Hormuz. The report said the market was again pricing geopolitical risk into energy and inflation expectations.

items.title: Treasury yields held steady as traders awaited U.S. data
items.summary: CNBC reported that U.S. Treasury yields steadied while investors waited for domestic economic releases after the earlier yield spike tied to the Middle East flare-up. The move suggested markets were in a cautious holding pattern rather than a broad risk-off rout.

items.title: IMF warned inflation risks remain elevated globally
items.summary: Financial Times coverage said the IMF raised its projections for price growth and warned that inflation could remain a major global threat. The same reporting also noted that some Fed officials saw the need for future rate rises to contain inflation.

items.title: Fed minutes showed lingering concern about inflation
items.summary: The Financial Times reported that minutes from the Federal Reserve's last meeting highlighted concern that price pressures remained high. That reinforces the view that policymakers are not yet fully comfortable easing policy.

items.title: U.S. economy added 57,000 jobs in June, below expectations
items.summary: MarketWatch and the Financial Times said the U.S. added 57,000 jobs in June and the unemployment rate fell to 4.2%. The report was weaker than many expected and did not appear likely to materially change the Fed's interest-rate stance.

items.title: ADP private payrolls rose by 98,000 in June
items.summary: MarketWatch reported that ADP estimated U.S. businesses created 98,000 jobs in June, the smallest increase in three months. The figure pointed to slower hiring momentum ahead of the official labor report.

items.title: China's producer inflation hit a near four-year high
items.summary: Reuters reported that China's producer prices rose for a fourth straight month in June, reaching their highest level since July 2022, while consumer prices also continued to rise. The data pointed to persistent cost pressure for manufacturers.

items.title: India inflation likely moved above the RBI's 4% target
items.summary: Reuters said a poll showed India's consumer inflation likely breached the Reserve Bank of India's 4% medium-term target in June for the first time in 16 months. Higher food and fuel prices were cited as key drivers.

items.title: OPEC+ agreed to a modest oil output increase for August
items.summary: Yahoo Finance reported that seven countries in the OPEC+ alliance agreed to raise combined output by 188,000 barrels per day in August. The increase came as crude prices were already sliding back from levels reached during the Iran-war spike.

items.title: India's rupee weakened and gold prices fell sharply
items.summary: Moneycontrol reported that the rupee opened lower and later traded in a wide range before closing weaker against the U.S. dollar. The same coverage said gold prices tumbled sharply as weak global cues reduced bullion demand.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Work for workplace automation
items.summary: OpenAI unveiled ChatGPT Work, an agent designed to execute tasks across applications and files, intensifying competition in professional AI tools. The company also said it is broadening its AI product lineup with a new focus on enterprise workflows.

items.title: OpenAI releases GPT-5.6 and a new real-time voice model family
items.summary: OpenAI broadly released GPT-5.6 and introduced GPT-Live, a family of voice models that can listen and speak simultaneously in real time. The releases reflect a continued push toward more capable general-purpose and multimodal AI systems.

items.title: Meta opens developer preview of Muse Spark 1.1
items.summary: Meta released developer access to Muse Spark 1.1, an upgraded AI model available through a public API preview. The move positions Meta more directly against Anthropic and OpenAI in monetizing model access.

items.title: OpenAI discontinues ChatGPT Atlas in favor of a desktop app
items.summary: OpenAI is reportedly ending ChatGPT Atlas, its standalone desktop browser, and shifting users toward the new ChatGPT desktop application. The change signals a consolidation of its desktop AI experience.

items.title: xAI launches Grok 4.5 for coding and agentic tasks
items.summary: xAI launched Grok 4.5, describing it as its most intelligent model yet and targeting coding and agentic tasks. The release adds to the rapid cycle of frontier model updates across major AI labs.

items.title: Anthropic appoints Ben Bernanke to Long-Term Benefit Trust
items.summary: Anthropic named former Federal Reserve chair Ben Bernanke to its Long-Term Benefit Trust, the oversight body meant to safeguard the company’s public-interest mission. The appointment highlights ongoing governance and safety positioning among major AI firms.

items.title: Italy fines Character.AI operator over data protection breaches
items.summary: Italy’s data protection authority fined Character Technologies, owner of Character.AI, €158,000 for violations of data protection rules. The case underscores growing regulatory scrutiny of consumer AI chatbots.

items.title: OpenAI faces new copyright dispute motion from major newspapers
items.summary: A group of newspapers including The New York Times asked a federal court to sanction OpenAI, alleging it misled the court about searching its systems for evidence in a copyright case. The dispute adds to legal pressure on AI training practices.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: PlayStation says it will end physical game disc production for new titles in January 2028
items.summary: Sony clarified that new PlayStation games released after January 2028 will be digital-only, with physical discs for new titles ending before then. The move is part of a broader shift away from physical media on PlayStation platforms.

items.title: Microsoft reportedly falls far short of its original Game Pass subscriber targets
items.summary: IGN reports that Microsoft expected Game Pass to reach 77 million subscribers by now, but it is reportedly around 30 million instead. The company’s gaming leadership has described the strategy as having failed to meet expectations.

items.title: Epic Games settles lawsuit with former Fortnite leaker
items.summary: Epic Games has reached a settlement in its case against former contractor Hayden Cohen, who was accused of leaking confidential Fortnite collaboration plans. The company dropped its monetary claims as part of the resolution.

items.title: Call of Duty: Black Ops 6 to become a standalone title outside Call of Duty HQ
items.summary: Activision is separating Black Ops 6 from the unified Call of Duty HQ launcher and making it run as its own dedicated game. The change is scheduled to take effect on July 7.

items.title: Nintendo to shut down Mario Kart Tour after seven years
items.summary: IGN reports that Nintendo will end service for Mario Kart Tour this September, with no offline version planned. The mobile racer will close after seven years online.

items.title: Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced draws strong early player counts on Steam
items.summary: IGN says the newly released Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced has reached about 100,000 concurrent players on Steam, setting a franchise record. The launch suggests unusually strong interest for the series on PC.

items.title: Resident Evil 2 remake overtakes Resident Evil 5 as the series’ best-selling game
items.summary: IGN’s latest report says the Resident Evil 2 remake has surpassed Resident Evil 5 to become the franchise’s top-selling entry, with roughly 19.75 million units sold. Capcom’s series total has now crossed 213 million copies worldwide.

items.title: Pokémon Go celebrates its 10th anniversary with a live event
items.summary: IGN is covering a live Pokémon Go 10th anniversary celebration event with announcements and surprises as they are revealed. The event marks a major milestone for the mobile game and its community.

tech_news.query: What are the most important technology news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major product launches, company news, and significant tech industry developments. Exclude AI-specific news.

items.title: Swift launches blockchain-based shared ledger for round-the-clock payments
items.summary: Global payments network Swift unveiled a blockchain-based shared ledger with 16 banks, including Citi and HSBC, aiming to support continuous cross-border payments and compete with stablecoin-based systems.

items.title: India removes import duty on key electronics and smartphone parts
items.summary: India scrapped import duties on some parts used in mobile phones and other electronics, a move that could lower manufacturing costs for companies such as Apple and Xiaomi.

items.title: Apple to spend more than $30 billion in Broadcom chip-supply agreement
items.summary: Apple said it will spend more than $30 billion under a chip-supply deal with Broadcom, which will also expand a factory in Colorado.

items.title: Meta plans in-house AI chip production from September
items.summary: Reuters reported that Meta plans to begin manufacturing an in-house AI chip in September as part of a broader effort to expand computing capacity.

items.title: EU lawmakers back interim rules on detecting child sexual abuse material
items.summary: European lawmakers backed a proposal to temporarily restore rules that would let platforms such as Google and Meta detect and remove child sexual abuse material online.

items.title: Meta launches in-house AI glasses line
items.summary: Meta announced a new line of AI glasses designed in-house, strengthening its push into wearables and consumer hardware.

items.title: US lifts export restrictions on Anthropic’s advanced Claude models
items.summary: The Trump administration lifted restrictions on Anthropic’s latest Claude chatbot versions after a weekslong ban tied to cybersecurity concerns.

items.title: South Korea plans massive chip manufacturing hub investment
items.summary: Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix plan a combined $518 billion investment in a new semiconductor manufacturing hub, reflecting strong demand tied to the broader chip cycle.

items.title: US government allows Anthropic model release to select users
items.summary: CNN reported that the US government has allowed Anthropic to release one of its powerful models to select companies and organizations after revising license requirements.

items.title: Major tech and chip stocks pressured by global selloff
items.summary: AP reported that Asian shares fell on heavy selling in computer chip stocks, following losses on Wall Street, signaling broader weakness in semiconductor markets.
